excerpt: External access: We will also continue to enable external research and government access for model releases to increase the depth of red-teaming and testing of frontier model capabilities
paraphrase: External research and government access will continue to be enabled for model releases to deepen red-teaming and testing.

excerpt: Safety drills: A critical part of this process is to be prepared if fast-moving emergency scenarios arise, including what default organizational response might look like (including how to stress-test against the pressures of our business or our culture).
paraphrase: Safety drills prepare the organization for fast-moving emergencies and define default responses, including stress-testing against business or cultural pressures.

excerpt: While the Preparedness team and SAG will of course work hard on forecasting and preparing for risks, safety drills can help the organization build “muscle memory” by practicing and coming up with the right “default” responses for some of the foreseeable scenarios.
paraphrase: Beyond forecasting efforts, safety drills build organizational muscle memory for foreseeable emergency scenarios.

excerpt: Therefore, the SAG will call for safety drills at a recommended minimum yearly basis
paraphrase: The SAG will call for safety drills at least annually as a recommended minimum.

excerpt: For each of these accountability measures, decision-making will follow the standard process (i.e., SAG chair synthesizes final recommendation, which OpenAI leadership makes a final decision on, that the BoD can overrule if needed).
paraphrase: Accountability measures follow the standard decision process: SAG Chair recommends, Leadership decides, Board can overrule.

excerpt: The Preparedness team monthly report updates the Scorecard pre-mitigation risk level in persuasion to “high” for a model that has just been trained.
paraphrase: A monthly Preparedness report updates the persuasion pre-mitigation risk level to 'high' for a newly trained model.

excerpt: This report includes a case with evidence from evaluations.
paraphrase: The report includes a case supported by evaluation evidence.

excerpt: The SAG Chair accepts the evidence supporting this new risk level, which would trigger two safety baselines: (1) to not continue with the deployment of the pre-mitigated model until mitigations are in place to ensure the post-mitigation risk will be at most “medium,” and (2) to ensure security measures are in place to prevent exfiltration by relevant actors; in this case, that would likely include foreign disinformation groups.
paraphrase: The SAG Chair accepts the evidence, triggering deployment restriction until post-mitigation risk reaches medium, and exfiltration security measures against relevant actors like foreign disinformation groups.

excerpt: The Preparedness team consults with relevant teams about the recommended mitigations and puts together a final set of suggestions for how to ensure the model is back at “medium” risk, which the SAG agrees with.
paraphrase: The Preparedness team consults on mitigations and finalizes suggestions to bring risk back to medium, which the SAG approves.

excerpt: The SAG Chair escalates to OpenAI leadership for a final decision.
paraphrase: The SAG Chair escalates the matter to OpenAI leadership for final decision.

excerpt: All documentation is sent to both OpenAI Leadership and the BoD for visibility and potential review
paraphrase: Documentation is sent to both Leadership and the Board for visibility and potential review.

excerpt: OpenAI Leadership agrees that the new pre-mitigation level for persuasion would be “high,” and agrees with the SAG plan to ensure sufficient mitigations are in place.
paraphrase: OpenAI Leadership confirms the 'high' pre-mitigation level and agrees with the SAG's mitigation plan.

excerpt: The BoD does not overrule the decision.
paraphrase: The Board does not overrule the leadership decision.

excerpt: The SAG works with the Preparedness and Security teams to ensure baseline safety measures are in place
paraphrase: The SAG collaborates with Preparedness and Security teams to implement baseline safety measures.

excerpt: The Preparedness team continues regular evaluations of both the pre-mitigation and post-mitigation risk and determines that while the pre-mitigation risk is “high”, the mitigations are sufficient to put the post-mitigation risk at “medium.”
paraphrase: Ongoing evaluations confirm pre-mitigation risk remains high while mitigations bring post-mitigation risk down to medium.
